goal: Deliver a reusable installable CGKN Agent Kit that operates from arbitrary project directories while preserving the reviewed Provider generation and delivery contracts.
acceptance_criteria: Codex automation is explicit, ephemeral, read-only, schema-constrained, and fails visibly when the executable or authentication is unavailable.
Manual Agent drafts and Codex drafts pass through the same deterministic supervisor response and brief validation.
Package, unit, contract, Windows-path, and dry-run tests pass, with local Codex executable limitations reported honestly.
Project generation invokes only scripts/run_local_pipeline.py with a validated --codex-capability-brief and never stores API keys.
Project initialization writes only portable support configuration and a secret-ignored artifact directory under .cgkn.
The companion is an independently installable Python package with a cgkn-agent command that works from an arbitrary project directory.

quality_metrics.measure: formal provider and delivery route preservation
quality_metrics.target: kernel and provider contract tests pass without a new generation or delivery path
quality_metrics.method: existing kernel and formal provider test profiles

quality_metrics.measure: bounded Codex escalation usefulness and authority isolation
quality_metrics.target: a librarian-curated request and Codex response stay within configured budgets, preserve request identity, produce actionable guidance, and cannot assert formal evidence or delivery authority
quality_metrics.method: schema validation, deterministic contract tests, support-pipeline prompt tests, and an offline failed-generation replay

prevention: Confirm acceptance, interfaces, and applicable kernel constraints before implementation.
assurance: Review method, schema, skill, and repository instruction consistency.
Validate that support artifacts cannot authorize formal delivery PASS.
Review changed files against the kernel contract before integration.
control: Run targeted kernel and knowledge tests.
improvement: Record review findings and one bounded improvement experiment.

interface_expectations: cgkn-agent may create support artifacts only under the target project's .cgkn directory.
Automatic Codex supervision is ephemeral, read-only, schema-constrained, and advisory-only.
Generation delegates only to scripts/run_local_pipeline.py with a validated capability brief; Provider, validation, packaging, and delivery authorities remain unchanged.
Credentials are process-only and never accepted as command arguments or persisted by the companion.

feedback: The reusable CLI, manual Agent sealing, Provider handoff, wheel, and cross-project tests pass; automatic Codex remains unavailable because the discovered WindowsApps executable returns access denied.

worked: A standalone stdlib-only package reused the sealed supervisor and Provider facade without adding generation or delivery authority.
did_not_work: The Microsoft Store desktop Codex executable cannot be launched directly from this PowerShell environment.
experiments: Test a separately installed official Codex CLI or a repaired Windows app execution alias, then rerun cgkn-agent doctor and assist without changing the advisory contract.
